# nish/crypto/scram

The arithmetic of a SCRAM-SHA-256 client, as RFC 5802 §3 defines it with SHA-256 for `H` and `HMAC` (RFC 7677 §3):

```ts
import {
  scramSha256ClientProof,
  scramSha256SaltedPassword,
  scramSha256ServerSignature,
} from "nish/crypto/scram";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { scramSha256ClientProof, scramSha256SaltedPassword, scramSha256ServerSignature } from "nish/crypto/scram";

const salted: Secret<u8[]> | null = scramSha256SaltedPassword(password, salt, 4096);
if (salted !== null) {
  const proof: u8[] = scramSha256ClientProof(salted, authMessage);
  const expected: u8[] = scramSha256ServerSignature(salted, authMessage);
  wipe(salted);
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="scram​Sha256​Client​Proof" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#scramsha256clientproof">

ClientProof, the `p=` of the client-final message (RFC 5802 §3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="scram​Sha256​Salted​Password" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#scramsha256saltedpassword">

SaltedPassword, RFC 5802 §3's `Hi(password, salt, i)`: PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA-256 and a 32-byte output (§2.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="scram​Sha256​Server​Signature" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#scramsha256serversignature">

ServerSignature, what the server's `v=` must equal (RFC 5802 §3).

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

```text
SaltedPassword  := Hi(Normalize(password), salt, i)
ClientKey       := HMAC(SaltedPassword, "Client Key")
StoredKey       := H(ClientKey)
ClientSignature := HMAC(StoredKey, AuthMessage)
ClientProof     := ClientKey XOR ClientSignature
ServerKey       := HMAC(SaltedPassword, "Server Key")
ServerSignature := HMAC(ServerKey, AuthMessage)
```

</scalar-callout>

The module holds none of SCRAM's messages: the caller builds AuthMessage,
decodes the server's salt and encodes the proof, so that a driver keeps its
own wire format and this file stays a pure function of its inputs, which a
contract (`specs/scram-sha256.md`) can hold to the RFC's printed exchange.
`Normalize` (SASLprep) is the caller's too: the password arrives as the
bytes the caller decided to send.

SaltedPassword, ClientKey and ServerKey each let whoever holds them log in
as the user, so SaltedPassword is taken and given as a `Secret`, and
ClientKey, StoredKey, ClientSignature and ServerKey are wiped before each
function returns. ClientProof and ServerSignature cross the wire in the
clear and are plain bytes. A caller compares the server's signature with
`timingSafeEqual` (`nish/crypto/ct`), and caps the iteration count before
it calls: `i=` is the server's to choose and Hi runs that many HMACs.

## Functions

### scramSha256ClientProof

ClientProof, the `p=` of the client-final message (RFC 5802 §3). ClientKey,
StoredKey and ClientSignature are wiped before it returns.

```ts
const scramSha256ClientProof: (
  saltedPassword: Secret<u8[]>,
  authMessage: u8[],
) => u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="saltedPassword" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

SaltedPassword from `scramSha256SaltedPassword`, read
  only inside `exposeWith`; still the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="authMessage" type="u8[]" required>

The client-first message without its GS2 header, the
  server-first message and the client-final message without its proof,
  joined by commas.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The 32-byte proof, which is sent in the clear.

</scalar-field>

### scramSha256SaltedPassword

SaltedPassword, RFC 5802 §3's `Hi(password, salt, i)`: PBKDF2 with
HMAC-SHA-256 and a 32-byte output (§2.2).

The time is linear in `iterations` and nothing here bounds it, so a caller
taking the count from a server caps it first.

```ts
const scramSha256SaltedPassword: (
  password: Secret<u8[]>,
  salt: u8[],
  iterations: i32,
) => Secret<u8[]> | null
```

<scalar-field name="password" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The password, already normalized as the caller sends it;
  read only inside `exposeWith`, and still the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="salt" type="u8[]" required>

The salt the server sent, decoded from base64.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="iterations" type="i32" required>

The server's iteration count `i`; below 1 answers `null`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt; | null">

SaltedPassword, which the caller wipes, or `null` when it cannot be
  computed.

</scalar-field>

### scramSha256ServerSignature

ServerSignature, what the server's `v=` must equal (RFC 5802 §3). ServerKey
is wiped before it returns. Compare it to the server's with
`timingSafeEqual`.

```ts
const scramSha256ServerSignature: (
  saltedPassword: Secret<u8[]>,
  authMessage: u8[],
) => u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="saltedPassword" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

SaltedPassword from `scramSha256SaltedPassword`, read
  only inside `exposeWith`; still the caller's to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="authMessage" type="u8[]" required>

The same AuthMessage the proof was computed over.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The 32-byte signature the server should send.

</scalar-field>
